findings.evidence: previous-version digest design-system-starter at dbff837f: 'removed units (485, showing 40)'. The digest is cut, so 445 removed units could not be checked one by one. All 40 shown units, both file: items and all 25 units of the be9701bf digest map to valid record rows.

For any unit with no row, restore it (into references/ when it is domain-specific, a template users ask for or a tested example) or add a row for it to docs/audit/recovery/design-system-starter/record.md.

findings.evidence: "files": [ "references/token-scales.md" ]. The token-scales-request, native-dialog-modal, touch-target-question and theme-toggle-no-flash evals list the skill's own reference files as eval input files.
findings.fix: Remove skill reference files from `files`. Give these evals only user inputs from evals/files/ (for example an existing tokens.json to extend, or an app shell for the theme toggle). That way the with-skill and without-skill runs differ only by the skill, and the assertions test whether the skill's loading triggers fire.

findings.evidence: "jsdom does not compute rendered colors, so jest-axe turns color contrast off ... axe's `color-contrast` rule checks text only". This states library defaults with no source URL and no check date.
findings.fix: Add the official sources and a checked date, for example the jest-axe README (https://github.com/nickcolley/jest-axe, color-contrast disabled by default) and the axe-core rule docs (https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/color-contrast). Or tell the agent to read the installed jest-axe and axe-core docs before relying on the default.

findings.evidence: dbff837f digest cut list: removed units (485, showing 40). The 40 shown paragraphs are explained by section rows in docs/audit/recovery/design-system-starter/sections.json plus record.md; the other 445 are not listed, so they cannot be ruled explained.

findings.evidence: description names DTCG .tokens.json and semantic tokens, but not the file shapes the workflow actually writes: design-tokens.json, $schema, CSS custom properties, or data-theme.
findings.fix: Set up or evolve a shared design system: semantic design tokens in a DTCG 2025.10 .tokens.json or design-tokens.json ($type, $value, $schema), CSS custom properties switched by data-theme for light and dark, reusable component APIs (atoms, molecules, organisms), contrast-checked token pairs, and versioned migration off scattered styles. Use when asked to create a design system or token file, convert raw hex, px or palette names into semantic tokens, standardize UI across apps or teams, define component library conventions, or version and deprecate shared tokens and components, even when the user only says the screens look inconsistent or all over the place. Not for reviewing or fixing one screen or component against UI rules (ui-ux-principles), one-off pages, ARIA how-to questions in an existing form, Storybook stories for existing components, SVG icon optimization, logos, or marketing copy.

findings.evidence: Step 7 says to run the theme-state check in references/component-examples.md, but does not say to load only the Theme-state validation section, and the file also holds Card, Modal, navigation and theme-toggle examples that step does not need.
findings.fix: In step 7, say to load only the Theme-state validation section of references/component-examples.md, and not the Card, Modal, navigation or theme-toggle sections, unless step 5 is also in scope.

findings.evidence: Step 6's default is data-theme CSS custom properties, but the escape hatch (Tailwind variants or a ThemeProvider) is chosen by whether the project already depends on it or needs runtime theme objects, with no tie-break when both are true.
findings.fix: Keep data-theme as the default; if both Tailwind and a ThemeProvider already exist, keep the one the consuming screens already use and record the choice in the checklist scope line.

findings.evidence: 19 trigger queries (10 should-trigger, 9 should-not), short of about 20 with 8-10 on each side, and no train/validation split.
findings.fix: Add one realistic should-not-trigger near-miss (for example a finished-token export or a one-file CSS rename) and mark a fixed 60/40 train/validation split in the query file.

findings.evidence: token-scales-request, native-dialog-modal, touch-target-question and theme-toggle-no-flash pass files references/token-scales.md, references/component-examples.md or references/component-specs.md, so they grade the bundled reference rather than the skill producing it from a user input.
findings.fix: Point those evals at user-owned inputs under evals/files/ (a partial token file, an existing non-native modal, a component list) and keep the references as the skill's own material, not as the prompt's file.

findings.evidence: The color-vision gotcha cites https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/rendering/apply-effects for Rendering tab > Emulate vision deficiencies. The recovery fact was checked against https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/accessibility/reference, and the registry row uses that page too.
findings.fix: Cite https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/accessibility/reference (the page that was checked on 2026-11-07), or re-check the rendering/apply-effects URL on this date and keep it only if Emulate vision deficiencies is actually documented there.

findings.evidence: The contrast script's worked example says #9ca3af on #fff prints ratio 2.5388 and pass false. The same relative-luminance formula yields about 2.54 only for the darker gray #9ca3af; #9ca3af on white is about 2.74, so the printed example is not what the script prints.
findings.fix: Re-run the script on #9ca3af and #fff and replace 2.5388 and 2.54 with the printed ratio and display values, keeping pass false.

findings.evidence: The naming rule says color.semantic.border.default becomes --color-border by dropping trailing default, but the deprecation example is rooted at color.action.default with no semantic segment, which the same rule would emit as --color-action-default, not --color-action.
findings.fix: State the rule for both shapes: a token under color.semantic drops semantic and a trailing default or ring, while a theme file rooted at color.action.default maps to --color-action.

findings.evidence: `timeout --foreground --kill-after=10s 1800 gemini -m gemini-3-pro-preview --approval-mode default -r "latest" "query"`: the follow-up command has no `cd`, unlike every other command shape, so `latest` can resolve against a different working directory than the original run

findings.evidence: Follow-up says to give `timeout --foreground --kill-after=10s 1800 gemini ... -r "latest" "query"` and, without confirmation that --resume combines with -p, to start a new headless run instead. The cited interactive form is `gemini -r "latest" "query"` with a positional prompt, which Gotchas says opens a waiting TTY session, so the proposed command is neither that form nor the headless fallback.
findings.fix: Give the documented interactive resume as `timeout --foreground --kill-after=10s 1800 gemini -m gemini-3-pro-preview --approval-mode default -i "query" -r latest` only if gemini --help shows -i and -r together; otherwise give only the new headless -p run that restates the accepted findings.
